always()/!cancelled()/failure() are rejected, but check-ci-needs.mjs:129 deliberately exempts success() ('success() is allowed; it is the default', :9). Per GitHub Actions semantics any status-check function in a job-level if: replaces the implicit success() check, so `if: ${{ success() || true }}`, `if: ${{ !success() }}` or `if: success() || github.event_name == 'push'` run the job after delivery-gates FAILED; all three pass the checker with OK/exit 0 (probes R1-R3). The finding's expected outcome ('fails any job whose if: uses ... other status functions, or otherwise proves each product job runs only when delivery-gates succeeded') is not met. Fix direction: reject any status function in a product job's if: except a bare `success()` / `success() && <expr>` form, or require no status function at all. (Static analysis; GitHub runtime behaviour per its documented expression semantics, not executed.)
